title: Jonah and the Parish
premise: When the coffin of Parish's founder, Augustin Voss, is exhumed for a centennial ceremony and found empty, night-shift taxi dispatcher Cyrus Joubert realizes the empty box matches a fare he logged five years ago—a woman everyone insists died the same week Voss was buried. As Cyrus digs through his alphabetized call records, he uncovers a conspiracy among the town's founding families, who faked both deaths to hide a drowning at the old cannery pier. The 'dead' witness, Mara Voss herself, has been hiding in plain sight as the parish organist, protected by Sheriff Dane Colter, who owes her his life. In the climax at the tide-flats, Cyrus must choose between turning over his evidence to the law that failed Mara or letting the sea keep its secret; he chooses truth on his own terms, broadcasting the dispatch tapes town-wide, and Mara walks free while the founders' empire collapses.
about_author: Gideon Almeida is the pen name of a former small-town radio operator who spent a decade listening to other people's emergencies before writing about them. He lives near a tidal marsh and still keeps meticulous logs.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Night
chapters.summary: Cyrus Joubert's POV. We meet him mid-shift, cataloguing fares and secrets in his ledger, invisible behind the dispatch headset. A routine call from the parish hall about the centennial exhumation lands on his desk. Emotional beat: quiet pride in being unseen, shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: Empty Box
chapters.summary: Cyrus attends the exhumation out of boredom and watches the crowd recoil: Augustin Voss's coffin holds only river stones. Sheriff Dane Colter's face goes white—not with shock, Cyrus thinks, but recognition. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the first crack in the town's polished surface.

chapters.title: Five Years of Fares
chapters.summary: Unable to sleep, Cyrus searches his old ledgers and finds it: the night Voss was buried, a fare from the cemetery gate to the cannery pier, logged under an alias—Mara Voss, officially dead three days prior. POV: Cyrus. Beat: dread mixed with the thrill of finally mattering.

chapters.title: The Widow's Tea
chapters.summary: Cyrus interviews Celeste Voss, the founder's widow, who performs grief flawlessly until he mentions river stones; her teacup shatters. She warns him off with a smile. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the realization that grief here is choreography.

chapters.title: Dispatch Tapes
chapters.summary: Cyrus pulls archived radio recordings and hears a second voice on the pier-night call—a man's, calm, directing the driver to wait. He recognizes the cadence: young Deputy Colter. POV: Cyrus. Beat: betrayal; the law itself is in the ledger.

chapters.title: Organ Music at Midnight
chapters.summary: Following a hunch, Cyrus sits in the back of evening mass and studies the organist, Ruth Ellery—whose hands tremble exactly like the woman he once glimpsed through a rain-streaked windshield five years ago. POV: Cyrus. Beat: hope sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Mara's POV: the drowning at the cannery pier, Augustin Voss alive and complicit, her staged death, Dane Colter carrying her from the water. Beat: terror, gratitude, and the bargain she struck.

chapters.title: A Debt in Uniform
chapters.summary: Dane Colter's POV. He confronts Cyrus at the dispatch office, offering promotion, silence, then threat. Cyrus pretends to fold; privately he copies the tape. Beat: two men circling, each hiding something.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus breaks into the historical society and finds the founding families' financial records: the cannery's closure hid a worker's death—Mara's brother—and payments funneled to keep mouths shut. POV: Cyrus. Beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading My Mail
chapters.summary: Cyrus returns to find his apartment searched, ledgers disturbed but nothing taken—a message. His cat is gone. POV: Cyrus. Beat: fear; invisibility was protection, and he's lost it.

chapters.title: Ruth Ellery Sings
chapters.summary: At a memorial service, the organist plays a hymn whose key changes match a phrase from the pier-night tape—a signal, Cyrus realizes, aimed at someone in the pews. He follows her home. POV: Cyrus. Beat: electric certainty.

chapters.title: Two Coffins
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She knows Cyrus knows. She prepares to run again, packing the one thing she kept: her brother's watch, recovered from the shallows. Beat: exhaustion of a woman who has been dead for five years.

chapters.title: The Pier at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Mara finally speak on the cannery pier. She tells him everything except who drove the getaway car. He promises nothing. POV alternates. Beat: wary tenderness—the book's love thread ignites against duty.

chapters.title: Colter's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Dane corners Cyrus again, this time drunk, nearly confessing his role before Celeste Voss calls him away. Cyrus records every slurred word. POV: Cyrus. Beat: pity warring with resolve.

chapters.title: The Driver
chapters.summary: Cyrus tracks down the retired cabbie who took the pier fare: old Amos Petit, dying, who admits he was paid by the founding families—and that the passenger wasn't fleeing, she was being exiled. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the conspiracy widens beyond one family.

chapters.title: Celeste Moves First
chapters.summary: Celeste Voss publicly accuses 'vandals' of the empty coffin and pushes to seal the case, while anonymously tipping the state police that Cyrus is harassing the widow. POV: Celeste. Beat: the antagonist strikes; Cyrus is now suspect.

chapters.title: Suspended Frequencies
chapters.summary: The taxi company suspends Cyrus pending investigation; his access to the archives is cut. Dane offers one last deal: hand over the tapes, leave town. POV: Cyrus. Beat: rock bottom—jobless, suspected, alone.

chapters.title: The Watch
chapters.summary: Mara makes her choice: she gives Cyrus her brother's watch, engraved with the date of the drowning, corroborating everything. They admit what they feel and agree to end it together. POV: Mara. Beat: love chosen over safety.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Celeste learns Mara lives and sends men to the tide-flats where Mara hides records. Cyrus races the incoming tide to reach them first, dispatching fake cab calls to misdirect the thugs. POV: Cyrus. Beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: from the dispatch console, Cyrus pipes the pier-night tapes, Amos's statement, and the founders' ledger entries over the town's emergency frequency during the centennial broadcast. The whole parish hears the truth at once. Beat: catharsis—justice outside the law, delivered on the airwaves.

chapters.title: What the Law Can Hold
chapters.summary: Fallout: Celeste and two founders are indicted; Dane resigns and testifies, shielding Mara by claiming he believed her dead. The state can't prosecute a ghost. POV: Dane. Beat: ruin, relief, and a debt half-paid.

chapters.title: First Fare
chapters.summary: Resolution: months later, Cyrus takes a last fare in his own cab—to the rebuilt pier, where Mara waits as the tide gives up the cannery's final secret: her brother's recovered effects. She signs a new name in his ledger. Beat: peace earned; two people no longer invisible to each other.
